description:
Run many person/location lookups in one call (row-in / row-out).

    Each row goes through the SAME engine as search_offenders, so a row's records
    are identical to what a single search would return. A row that fails is
    reported with status='error' in place and never aborts the batch. Max 1000 rows.

    Returns: { count, results: [ { index, status, counts{records,sourcesQueried,
    sourcesIncomplete}, warnings: [str], records: [Record], error? } ] } in input
    order. ★ A row with `counts.sourcesIncomplete > 0` could not be searched to the
    end — its `records` are a LOWER BOUND, not a clean 'no match'.

    Auth: uses the caller's X-API-Key (request header or OFFENDERSEARCH_API_KEY env).

extensive.description: Request extensive detail (offenses[], stateData, images) for every row.
extensive.title: Extensive

freshness.description: Cache/pricing tier applied to every row: daily=<=24h (default), weekly=<=7d.
freshness.title: Freshness

jurisdictions.description: Registry codes applied to EVERY row (e.g. ['FL','TX']). Omit = all 58 registries.
jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions

location_scoped.description: Apply per-state scoping to every row (see search_offenders).
location_scoped.title: Location Scoped

match.description: Fuzzy tolerance applied to every row (see search_offenders).
match.title: Match

queries.description: List of query objects (max 1000). Each may set any of: firstName, lastName, dob (YYYY-MM-DD), age, city, state, zipcode, address, lat, lng, radiusMiles, q. One row in = one result out, in input order.
queries.title: Queries

name: batch_search
